Probability forecasts as martingales

A sequence of forecasts for one event must agree about what future information can reveal. We first prove that conditional event probabilities form a martingale, then construct two diffusion models and derive a bound on expected squared revisions. The models also show why a claim about “more uncertainty” needs to specify which quantity changes.

The calibration page supplies the binary payoff and Brier score; probability conflation explains why event accuracy does not identify severity. Here the payoff is exactly one or zero. Source context is SCoFT v4, chapter 14, pp. 261–273 Taleb, 2025; the chapter guide records qualifications and locators. Every numerical example is synthetic.

One event, one probability law¶

The tower property establishes the conditional identity used below.

Proposition 1 (Conditional event probabilities are martingales)

Fix a probability space with law PPP, a finite horizon T≥0T\ge0T≥0, an increasing filtration (Ft)0≤t≤T(\mathcal F_t)_{0\le t\le T}(Ft​)0≤t≤T​, and an event A∈FTA\in\mathcal F_TA∈FT​. Define the report

pt=E[1A∣Ft].p_t=\mathbb E[\mathbf1_A\mid\mathcal F_t].pt​=E[1A​∣Ft​].
(1)

Then ppp is an [0,1][0,1][0,1]-valued martingale under PPP with pT=1Ap_T=\mathbf1_ApT​=1A​. It is also a martingale in the report filtration Gt=σ(pr:r≤t)\mathcal G_t=\sigma(p_r:r\le t)Gt​=σ(pr​:r≤t). Conversely, every (Ft)(\mathcal F_t)(Ft​)-martingale with terminal value 1A\mathbf1_A1A​ equals E[1A∣Ft]\mathbb E[\mathbf1_A\mid\mathcal F_t]E[1A​∣Ft​] at each time, almost surely.

Proof 1

Since 0≤1A≤10\le\mathbf1_A\le10≤1A​≤1, each ptp_tpt​ is integrable, adapted, and lies in [0,1][0,1][0,1]; A∈FTA\in\mathcal F_TA∈FT​ gives pT=1Ap_T=\mathbf1_ApT​=1A​. For s≤ts\le ts≤t, the tower property gives

E[pt∣Fs]=E[E[1A∣Ft]∣Fs]=E[1A∣Fs]=ps.\begin{aligned} \mathbb E[p_t\mid\mathcal F_s] &=\mathbb E[\mathbb E[\mathbf1_A\mid\mathcal F_t] \mid\mathcal F_s]\\ &=\mathbb E[\mathbf1_A\mid\mathcal F_s]=p_s. \end{aligned}E[pt​∣Fs​]​=E[E[1A​∣Ft​]∣Fs​]=E[1A​∣Fs​]=ps​.​
(2)

This proves the claim under the forecaster’s own law. It also holds in the smaller filtration Gt=σ(pr:r≤t)\mathcal G_t=\sigma(p_r:r\le t)Gt​=σ(pr​:r≤t) generated by the reports: apply the tower property again, using psp_sps​’s Gs\mathcal G_sGs​-measurability. Conversely, an adapted martingale with terminal value 1A\mathbf1_A1A​ has pt=E[1A∣Ft]p_t=\mathbb E[\mathbf1_A\mid\mathcal F_t]pt​=E[1A​∣Ft​] by its defining identity.

A filtration records all information retained by the forecaster at each time. The shared notation uses PPP for the law and E\mathbb EE for its expectation. Our local ptp_tpt​ is an event probability, not a density. Conditional expectations are understood up to almost-sure equality. Boundedness or a constant unconditional mean alone does not imply this conditional identity.

The claim requires the same event, law, and nested information sets. Replacing the event, forgetting information, or changing the model without embedding that change in one joint law does not satisfy these assumptions. Ordinary conditional expectation is the only prerequisite; see the conditional-expectation note.

Fair bets, scores, and market prices¶

We prove two finite-horizon consequences of Proposition 1.

Corollary 1 (Fair predictable bets and optimal conditional Brier reports)

Let PPP be a probability law, (Ft)0≤t≤T(\mathcal F_t)_{0\le t\le T}(Ft​)0≤t≤T​ an increasing filtration with T>0T>0T>0, A∈FTA\in\mathcal F_TA∈FT​, and pt=EP[1A∣Ft]p_t=\mathbb E_P[\mathbf1_A\mid\mathcal F_t]pt​=EP​[1A​∣Ft​]. On a deterministic grid 0≤t0<⋯<tm=T0\le t_0<\cdots<t_m=T0≤t0​<⋯<tm​=T, let hih_ihi​ be a bounded Fti\mathcal F_{t_i}Fti​​-measurable position. A purchase of hih_ihi​ units at ptip_{t_i}pti​​, unwound at the next quote, has gain

Δpi=pti+1−pti,G=∑i=0m−1hiΔpi,E[hiΔpi]=0,E[G]=0.\begin{gathered} \Delta p_i=p_{t_{i+1}}-p_{t_i},\\ G=\sum_{i=0}^{m-1}h_i\Delta p_i,\\ \mathbb E[h_i\Delta p_i]=0,\qquad \mathbb E[G]=0. \end{gathered}Δpi​=pti+1​​−pti​​,G=i=0∑m−1​hi​Δpi​,E[hi​Δpi​]=0,E[G]=0.​
(3)

Thus GGG cannot be nonnegative almost surely and positive with positive probability. Interpreting GGG as trading profit assumes two-way execution at the quotes, no transaction costs, zero financing rate, and self-financing trades.

For an Ft\mathcal F_tFt​-measurable report qt∈[0,1]q_t\in[0,1]qt​∈[0,1], the conditional Brier loss satisfies

E[(1A−qt)2∣Ft]=pt(1−pt)+(qt−pt)2.\begin{aligned} \mathbb E[(\mathbf1_A-q_t)^2\mid\mathcal F_t] &=p_t(1-p_t)\\ &\quad+(q_t-p_t)^2. \end{aligned}E[(1A​−qt​)2∣Ft​]​=pt​(1−pt​)+(qt​−pt​)2.​
(4)

Its unique minimizing report is qt=ptq_t=p_tqt​=pt​, up to almost-sure equality.

Proof 2

By Proposition 1, E[Δpi∣Fti]=0\mathbb E[\Delta p_i\mid\mathcal F_{t_i}]=0E[Δpi​∣Fti​​]=0. Multiply by the bounded Fti\mathcal F_{t_i}Fti​​-measurable hih_ihi​, take expectations, and sum to get EG=0\mathbb E G=0EG=0. An integrable nonnegative gain that is positive with positive probability would have positive expectation. For the Brier identity, expand the square and substitute E[1A∣Ft]=pt\mathbb E[\mathbf1_A\mid\mathcal F_t]=p_tE[1A​∣Ft​]=pt​ to prove it. The nonnegative remainder (qt−pt)2(q_t-p_t)^2(qt​−pt​)2 vanishes exactly at qt=ptq_t=p_tqt​=pt​.

Thus optimal conditional quadratic scoring and dynamic fair betting select the same conditional probability under the specified law. Linear trading profit is not itself a strictly proper score. The no-free-lunch consequence is for bounded predictable positions; it says nothing about unbounded doubling strategies.

De Finetti’s probability-assessor connection is that the quoted probability is a price at which either side of a unit event bet is acceptable. For finitely many fair bets, a common expectation precludes a strictly positive gain in every outcome. This is the implication from probability coherence to fair betting, not a proof of the full representation theorem for coherent assessments. Chapter 14, §14.3, pp. 269–271 supplies the historical connection Taleb, 2025.

A traded claim can instead be valued under a pricing law QQQ. If its discounted price is a conditional expectation under QQQ, the martingale identity is under QQQ; identifying QQQ with a physical or subjective law PPP is an additional assumption. Complementary prices summing to one do not force that identification. A predictable positive expected gain under PPP can still incur losses, so it is not automatically an arbitrage. For example, if P(A)=0.6P(A)=0.6P(A)=0.6 but two complementary claims both cost 0.5, their prices sum to one. Buying the first has expected gain 0.1 under PPP, but loses 0.5 when the event fails.

Gaussian terminal uncertainty¶

The normal transition law gives both the event probability and its sensitivities.

Proposition 2 (Gaussian binary probabilities and sensitivities)

Let Xt=x0+σWtX_t=x_0+\sigma W_tXt​=x0​+σWt​ with x0∈Rx_0\in\mathbb Rx0​∈R, constant σ>0\sigma>0σ>0, and standard Brownian motion WWW under PPP with its usual filtration. Fix T>0T>0T>0, u∈Ru\in\mathbb Ru∈R, and A={XT>u}A=\{X_T>u\}A={XT​>u}. For 0≤t<T0\le t<T0≤t<T, write τ=T−t\tau=T-tτ=T−t, s=στs=\sigma\sqrt\taus=στ​, and d=(x−u)/sd=(x-u)/sd=(x−u)/s. With Φ\PhiΦ the standard normal CDF and ϕ=Φ′\phi=\Phi'ϕ=Φ′ its density,

XT∣Xt=x ∼N(x,s2),p(t,x)=P(A∣Xt=x)=Φ(d).\begin{gathered} X_T\mid X_t=x\ \sim N(x,s^2),\\ p(t,x)=P(A\mid X_t=x)=\Phi(d). \end{gathered}XT​∣Xt​=x ∼N(x,s2),p(t,x)=P(A∣Xt​=x)=Φ(d).​
(5)

The sensitivities, holding the other independent arguments fixed, are

∂p∂s=−dϕ(d)s,∂p∂x=ϕ(d)s,∂p∂τ=−dϕ(d)2τ.\begin{gathered} \frac{\partial p}{\partial s} =-\frac{d\phi(d)}{s},\\ \frac{\partial p}{\partial x} =\frac{\phi(d)}{s},\qquad \frac{\partial p}{\partial\tau} =-\frac{d\phi(d)}{2\tau}. \end{gathered}∂s∂p​=−sdϕ(d)​,∂x∂p​=sϕ(d)​,∂τ∂p​=−2τdϕ(d)​.​
(6)

At fixed x,ux,ux,u, increasing sss moves ppp toward 1/21/21/2, with limit 1/21/21/2 as s→∞s\to\inftys→∞. The level sensitivity ϕ(d)/s\phi(d)/sϕ(d)/s tends to zero as s→∞s\to\inftys→∞, increases for s<∣x−u∣s<|x-u|s<∣x−u∣, and decreases for s>∣x−u∣s>|x-u|s>∣x−u∣. At fixed x≠ux\ne ux=u and σ\sigmaσ, ppp tends to 1{x>u}\mathbf1_{\{x>u\}}1{x>u}​ as τ↓0\tau\downarrow0τ↓0; at x=ux=ux=u and positive sss, it equals 1/21/21/2. For t<Tt<Tt<T, the forecast process has zero drift and satisfies

dp(t,Xt)=ϕ((Xt−u)/(σT−t))T−t dWt.dp(t,X_t)=\frac{\phi((X_t-u)/(\sigma\sqrt{T-t}))}{\sqrt{T-t}}\,dW_t.dp(t,Xt​)=T−t​ϕ((Xt​−u)/(σT−t​))​dWt​.
(7)

At fixed x,u∈Rx,u\in\mathbb Rx,u∈R and τ>0\tau>0τ>0, this diffusion coefficient is independent of σ\sigmaσ at x=ux=ux=u; away from the threshold, it increases with σ\sigmaσ toward ϕ(0)/τ\phi(0)/\sqrt\tauϕ(0)/τ​.

Proof 3

Independent Brownian increments give the conditional normal law. Standardizing XT>uX_T>uXT​>u and using normal symmetry gives p=Φ(d)p=\Phi(d)p=Φ(d). Differentiation gives the three partial derivatives. Also, ∂s[ϕ(d)/s]=(d2−1)ϕ(d)/s2\partial_s[\phi(d)/s]=(d^2-1)\phi(d)/s^2∂s​[ϕ(d)/s]=(d2−1)ϕ(d)/s2, which proves the stated monotonicity of the level sensitivity. The limits follow from d=(x−u)/sd=(x-u)/sd=(x−u)/s and continuity of Φ\PhiΦ and ϕ\phiϕ. Itô’s formula gives diffusion coefficient σ∂xp=ϕ(d)/τ\sigma\partial_xp=\phi(d)/\sqrt\tauσ∂x​p=ϕ(d)/τ​. Its drift is zero: ∂tp=dϕ(d)/(2τ)\partial_t p=d\phi(d)/(2\tau)∂t​p=dϕ(d)/(2τ) and ∂xxp=−dϕ(d)/s2\partial_{xx}p=-d\phi(d)/s^2∂xx​p=−dϕ(d)/s2 cancel in ∂tp+σ2∂xxp/2\partial_t p+\sigma^2\partial_{xx}p/2∂t​p+σ2∂xx​p/2. At fixed x,u,τx,u,\taux,u,τ, increasing σ\sigmaσ decreases ∣d∣|d|∣d∣ toward zero; the normal density then increases to ϕ(0)\phi(0)ϕ(0), unless d=0d=0d=0 throughout.

This is the undiscounted value of a binary Bachelier claim. As a local approximation to a vote-share estimate, the model allows values outside [0,1][0,1][0,1]; it is not an exactly bounded share process. At zero variance we use the strict-event value 1{x>u}\mathbf1_{\{x>u\}}1{x>u}​, including zero at the tie; that degenerate case differs from the positive-variance limit.

Sensitivity to the underlying level is not the same as the forecast’s instantaneous volatility. There is therefore no universal rule that a higher underlying volatility lowers forecast-path volatility.

Use gaussian_binary_probability to compare remaining horizons and the deterministic boundary.

from xmath.incerto.martingales import gaussian_binary_probability

for tau in (1, .25, .01, 0):
    p = gaussian_binary_probability(.54, .08, tau)
    print(f"time left={tau:.2f}: probability={p:.3f}")
print(f"deterministic tie: {gaussian_binary_probability(.5, 0, 1):.1f}")

Output

time left=1.00: probability=0.691
time left=0.25: probability=0.841
time left=0.01: probability=1.000
time left=0.00: probability=1.000
deterministic tie: 0.0

An exactly bounded share process¶

We now construct a different model. Write Yt∈(0,1)Y_t\in(0,1)Yt​∈(0,1) for the share; YYY is local to this page, not the positive mixing variable of the Normix notation. Its unbounded coordinate is Zt=Φ−1(Yt)Z_t=\Phi^{-1}(Y_t)Zt​=Φ−1(Yt​).

Proposition 3 (A bounded probit martingale)

Fix σ>0\sigma>0σ>0, deterministic z0∈Rz_0\in\mathbb Rz0​∈R, and standard Brownian motion WWW under PPP with its usual filtration (Ft)(\mathcal F_t)(Ft​). Let Φ,ϕ\Phi,\phiΦ,ϕ be the standard normal CDF and density, and define

Zt=eσ2t/2(z0+σ∫0te−σ2r/2 dWr),Yt=Φ(Zt).\begin{gathered} Z_t=e^{\sigma^2t/2}\left(z_0+\sigma \int_0^t e^{-\sigma^2r/2}\,dW_r\right),\\ Y_t=\Phi(Z_t). \end{gathered}Zt​=eσ2t/2(z0​+σ∫0t​e−σ2r/2dWr​),Yt​=Φ(Zt​).​
(8)

Then ZZZ solves dZt=12σ2Zt dt+σ dWtdZ_t=\tfrac12\sigma^2Z_t\,dt+\sigma\,dW_tdZt​=21​σ2Zt​dt+σdWt​ and is finite at every finite time. For t≥0t\ge0t≥0 and h>0h>0h>0, conditional on Ft\mathcal F_tFt​ with Zt=zZ_t=zZt​=z,

Zt+h∼N(eσ2h/2z, eσ2h−1).Z_{t+h}\sim N(e^{\sigma^2h/2}z,\ e^{\sigma^2h}-1).Zt+h​∼N(eσ2h/2z, eσ2h−1).
(9)

The second normal parameter is the variance. The process YYY stays in (0,1)(0,1)(0,1) and is a true martingale with dYt=σϕ(Zt) dWtdY_t=\sigma\phi(Z_t)\,dW_tdYt​=σϕ(Zt​)dWt​. The coordinate ZZZ is not a martingale: for h>0h>0h>0, E[Zt+h∣Ft]=eσ2h/2Zt\mathbb E[Z_{t+h}\mid\mathcal F_t]=e^{\sigma^2h/2}Z_tE[Zt+h​∣Ft​]=eσ2h/2Zt​, which differs from ZtZ_tZt​ almost surely at every t>0t>0t>0.

Proof 4

The integrating-factor formula gives the SDE and finiteness of ZZZ. Independent Brownian increments give the conditional normal mean; integrating σ2eσ2(h−r)\sigma^2e^{\sigma^2(h-r)}σ2eσ2(h−r) over 0≤r≤h0\le r\le h0≤r≤h gives its variance. Since Φ\PhiΦ maps finite reals to (0,1)(0,1)(0,1), YYY stays bounded. For independent standard normals H,NH,NH,N, any real bbb and c≥0c\ge0c≥0,

E[Φ(b+cN)]=P(H−cN≤b)=Φ ⁣(b1+c2).\begin{aligned} \mathbb E[\Phi(b+cN)] &=P(H-cN\le b)\\ &=\Phi\!\left(\frac{b}{\sqrt{1+c^2}}\right). \end{aligned}E[Φ(b+cN)]​=P(H−cN≤b)=Φ(1+c2​b​).​
(10)

Take b=eσ2h/2zb=e^{\sigma^2h/2}zb=eσ2h/2z and c2=eσ2h−1c^2=e^{\sigma^2h}-1c2=eσ2h−1. The denominator is eσ2h/2e^{\sigma^2h/2}eσ2h/2, so E[Yt+h∣Ft]=Φ(z)=Yt\mathbb E[Y_{t+h}\mid\mathcal F_t]=\Phi(z)=Y_tE[Yt+h​∣Ft​]=Φ(z)=Yt​. This proves a true bounded martingale directly from its transition law, without assuming that a nonlinear transform preserves martingales. Itô’s formula gives the equivalent drift cancellation:

ϕ′(z)=−zϕ(z),12σ2zϕ(z)+12σ2ϕ′(z)=0,dYt=σϕ(Zt) dWt.\begin{gathered} \phi'(z)=-z\phi(z),\\ \tfrac12\sigma^2z\phi(z)+\tfrac12\sigma^2\phi'(z)=0,\\ dY_t=\sigma\phi(Z_t)\,dW_t. \end{gathered}ϕ′(z)=−zϕ(z),21​σ2zϕ(z)+21​σ2ϕ′(z)=0,dYt​=σϕ(Zt​)dWt​.​
(11)

Only YYY is a martingale here. The transition mean gives E[Zt+h∣Ft]=eσ2h/2Zt\mathbb E[Z_{t+h}\mid\mathcal F_t]=e^{\sigma^2h/2}Z_tE[Zt+h​∣Ft​]=eσ2h/2Zt​. At t>0t>0t>0, ZtZ_tZt​ is a nondegenerate normal, so Zt≠0Z_t\ne0Zt​=0 almost surely and the conditional martingale equality fails.

The drift of ZZZ is directed away from zero. Even starting at z0=0z_0=0z0​=0 makes just its unconditional mean constant.

The drift cancellation extends to other smooth increasing transforms.

Proposition 4 (Drift adjustment for a bounded transform)

Let S:R→(0,1)S:\mathbb R\to(0,1)S:R→(0,1) be increasing, twice continuously differentiable, and have S′>0S'>0S′>0. For a nonexplosive adapted solution of dZt=b(Zt)dt+σdWtdZ_t=b(Z_t)dt+\sigma dW_tdZt​=b(Zt​)dt+σdWt​ on a fixed finite horizon, where WWW is standard Brownian motion and σ>0\sigma>0σ>0 is constant, suppose

b(z)=−σ2S′′(z)2S′(z).b(z)=-\frac{\sigma^2S''(z)}{2S'(z)}.b(z)=−2S′(z)σ2S′′(z)​.
(12)

Then S(Zt)S(Z_t)S(Zt​) is a true bounded martingale and dS(Zt)=σS′(Zt) dWtdS(Z_t)=\sigma S'(Z_t)\,dW_tdS(Zt​)=σS′(Zt​)dWt​.

Proof 5

Itô’s drift is b(Zt)S′(Zt)+σ2S′′(Zt)/2=0b(Z_t)S'(Z_t)+\sigma^2S''(Z_t)/2=0b(Zt​)S′(Zt​)+σ2S′′(Zt​)/2=0. Localizing the resulting stochastic integral makes S(Z)S(Z)S(Z) a local martingale; its bound by one allows dominated convergence in the stopped conditional identities, making it a true martingale.

This assertion assumes the solution exists without explosion on the horizon. For the logistic S(z)=(1+e−z)−1S(z)=(1+e^{-z})^{-1}S(z)=(1+e−z)−1 the required drift is b(z)=σ2(2S(z)−1)/2b(z)=\sigma^2(2S(z)-1)/2b(z)=σ2(2S(z)−1)/2, which is bounded and globally Lipschitz. A sigmoid applied to driftless Brownian motion generally has nonzero Itô drift. Symmetry at its starting point does not remove that drift along subsequent paths.

For a direct counterexample, the probit transform of driftless Brownian motion has a constant mean but fails the conditional identity.

Proposition 5 (Constant mean without the martingale property)

Let WWW be standard Brownian motion with its usual filtration (Ft)(\mathcal F_t)(Ft​), σ>0\sigma>0σ>0, Zt=σWtZ_t=\sigma W_tZt​=σWt​, and Yt=Φ(Zt)Y_t=\Phi(Z_t)Yt​=Φ(Zt​), where Φ\PhiΦ is the standard normal CDF. For t≥0t\ge0t≥0 and h>0h>0h>0,

E[Yt]=1/2,E[Yt+h∣Ft]=Φ ⁣(Zt1+σ2h).\begin{gathered} \mathbb E[Y_t]=1/2,\\ \mathbb E[Y_{t+h}\mid\mathcal F_t] =\Phi\!\left(\frac{Z_t}{\sqrt{1+\sigma^2h}}\right). \end{gathered}E[Yt​]=1/2,E[Yt+h​∣Ft​]=Φ(1+σ2h​Zt​​).​
(13)

Thus YYY is not a martingale despite its constant unconditional mean.

Proof 6

Symmetry gives EΦ(Zt)=1/2\mathbb E\Phi(Z_t)=1/2EΦ(Zt​)=1/2. Conditional on Ft\mathcal F_tFt​, Zt+h=Zt+σh NZ_{t+h}=Z_t+\sigma\sqrt h\,NZt+h​=Zt​+σh​N with NNN an independent standard normal. The normal integration identity in the proof of Proposition 3 gives the conditional mean. At any t>0t>0t>0, Zt≠0Z_t\ne0Zt​=0 almost surely, so strict monotonicity of Φ\PhiΦ makes that mean differ from YtY_tYt​.

The midpoint exception concerns the unconditional mean, not the martingale property.

The event probability is a second martingale¶

The transition law gives the event probability for the bounded share process.

Corollary 2 (Event forecasts in the bounded probit model)

Let Z,YZ,YZ,Y be the processes in Proposition 3, fix T>0T>0T>0 and 0<u<10<u<10<u<1, and set k=Φ−1(u)k=\Phi^{-1}(u)k=Φ−1(u) and A={YT>u}A=\{Y_T>u\}A={YT​>u}. For 0≤t<T0\le t<T0≤t<T, τ=T−t\tau=T-tτ=T−t, and 0<y<10<y<10<y<1,

z=Φ−1(y),p(t,y)=P(A∣Yt=y)=Φ ⁣(z−e−σ2τ/2k1−e−σ2τ).\begin{gathered} z=\Phi^{-1}(y),\\ p(t,y)=P(A\mid Y_t=y)=\Phi\!\left( \frac{z-e^{-\sigma^2\tau/2}k} {\sqrt{1-e^{-\sigma^2\tau}}}\right). \end{gathered}z=Φ−1(y),p(t,y)=P(A∣Yt​=y)=Φ(1−e−σ2τ​z−e−σ2τ/2k​).​
(14)

The process p(t,Yt)p(t,Y_t)p(t,Yt​), extended at TTT by 1A\mathbf1_A1A​, is the conditional probability of AAA given Ft\mathcal F_tFt​ and is a martingale.

For a majority threshold u=1/2u=1/2u=1/2, k=0k=0k=0. At fixed interior share yyy, increasing the integrated latent variance σ2τ\sigma^2\tauσ2τ moves p(t,y)p(t,y)p(t,y) toward yyy, and

lim⁡σ2τ→∞p(t,y)=y.\lim_{\sigma^2\tau\to\infty}p(t,y)=y.σ2τ→∞lim​p(t,y)=y.
(15)

For y>1/2y>1/2y>1/2 the forecast lies between yyy and one; for y<1/2y<1/2y<1/2 it lies between zero and yyy; for y=1/2y=1/2y=1/2 it equals 1/21/21/2. The same limit holds for every fixed 0<u<10<u<10<u<1, without a general monotonicity assertion.

Proof 7

Monotonicity makes AAA exactly {ZT>k}\{Z_T>k\}{ZT​>k}. Standardize the conditional normal law in Proposition 3, dividing its mean, threshold, and standard deviation by eσ2τ/2e^{\sigma^2\tau/2}eσ2τ/2. This gives the displayed formula, including conditioning on the full Ft\mathcal F_tFt​. The martingale claim follows from Proposition 1. For k=0k=0k=0, the denominator increases to one, so the argument of Φ\PhiΦ approaches zzz. For y>1/2y>1/2y>1/2 the forecast stays between yyy and one; for y<1/2y<1/2y<1/2 it stays between zero and yyy. For any fixed interior threshold the same limit holds because e−σ2τ/2k→0e^{-\sigma^2\tau/2}k\to0e−σ2τ/2k→0, although monotonicity in σ2τ\sigma^2\tauσ2τ need not.

The share YtY_tYt​ has terminal value YTY_TYT​, so the share and event forecast are different martingales. Neither statement makes ZtZ_tZt​ a martingale. Computing the event in either coordinate must give the same probability; the threshold must be transformed as well. This bounded model therefore does not have a universal 1/21/21/2 limit. Its increasing terminal dispersion preserves the mean share, unlike an unbounded normal approximation with arbitrarily large variance.

Use probit_binary_probability for the bounded model. The noise parameter is in the latent coordinate; it is not the share’s instantaneous volatility, which is σϕ(Φ−1(y))\sigma\phi(\Phi^{-1}(y))σϕ(Φ−1(y)).

from xmath.incerto.martingales import probit_binary_probability

for sigma in (.2, .6, 2, 10):
    p = probit_binary_probability(.54, sigma, 1)
    print(f"latent scale={sigma:.1f}: probability={p:.3f}")

Output

latent scale=0.2: probability=0.694
latent scale=0.6: probability=0.572
latent scale=2.0: probability=0.540
latent scale=10.0: probability=0.540

How much revision is coherent?¶

Return to any conditional binary forecast, without a diffusion assumption. We prove the conditional revision budget and its Brier interpretation.

Proposition 6 (Squared-revision budget and Brier improvement)

Let A∈FTA\in\mathcal F_TA∈FT​, where (Ft)0≤t≤T(\mathcal F_t)_{0\le t\le T}(Ft​)0≤t≤T​ is an increasing filtration under PPP. On a deterministic grid 0≤t0<⋯<tm≤T0\le t_0<\cdots<t_m\le T0≤t0​<⋯<tm​≤T, set pi=E[1A∣Fti]p_i=\mathbb E[\mathbf1_A\mid\mathcal F_{t_i}]pi​=E[1A​∣Fti​​], Δpi=pi+1−pi\Delta p_i=p_{i+1}-p_iΔpi​=pi+1​−pi​, and V=∑i=0m−1(Δpi)2V=\sum_{i=0}^{m-1}(\Delta p_i)^2V=∑i=0m−1​(Δpi​)2. Then

E[V∣Ft0]=p0(1−p0)−E[pm(1−pm)∣Ft0]≤p0(1−p0).\mathbb E[V\mid\mathcal F_{t_0}] =p_0(1-p_0)-\mathbb E[p_m(1-p_m)\mid\mathcal F_{t_0}] \le p_0(1-p_0).E[V∣Ft0​​]=p0​(1−p0​)−E[pm​(1−pm​)∣Ft0​​]≤p0​(1−p0​).
(16)

If tm=Tt_m=Ttm​=T, the budget is exactly

E[V∣Ft0]=p0(1−p0).\mathbb E[V\mid\mathcal F_{t_0}]=p_0(1-p_0).E[V∣Ft0​​]=p0​(1−p0​).
(17)

For every 0≤i<m0\le i<m0≤i<m,

E[(1A−pi)2]−E[(1A−pi+1)2]=E[(Δpi)2].\begin{gathered} \mathbb E[(\mathbf1_A-p_i)^2] -\mathbb E[(\mathbf1_A-p_{i+1})^2]\\ =\mathbb E[(\Delta p_i)^2]. \end{gathered}E[(1A​−pi​)2]−E[(1A​−pi+1​)2]=E[(Δpi​)2].​
(18)
Proof 8

Expand pi+12−pi2=2piΔpi+(Δpi)2p_{i+1}^2-p_i^2=2p_i\Delta p_i+(\Delta p_i)^2pi+12​−pi2​=2pi​Δpi​+(Δpi​)2. By Proposition 1, the cross term has conditional mean zero. Sum and condition at t0t_0t0​ to get E[V∣Ft0]=E[pm2∣Ft0]−p02\mathbb E[V\mid\mathcal F_{t_0}] =\mathbb E[p_m^2\mid\mathcal F_{t_0}]-p_0^2E[V∣Ft0​​]=E[pm2​∣Ft0​​]−p02​. Since E[pm∣Ft0]=p0\mathbb E[p_m\mid\mathcal F_{t_0}]=p_0E[pm​∣Ft0​​]=p0​, this is the general budget. At resolution pm=1Ap_m=\mathbf1_Apm​=1A​, so pm(1−pm)=0p_m(1-p_m)=0pm​(1−pm​)=0. For the Brier identity, expand 1A−pi=(1A−pi+1)+Δpi\mathbf1_A-p_i=(\mathbf1_A-p_{i+1})+\Delta p_i1A​−pi​=(1A​−pi+1​)+Δpi​ and condition the cross term on Fti+1\mathcal F_{t_{i+1}}Fti+1​​; its mean is zero.

If the grid stops before resolution, its expected squared revisions, conditional on Ft0\mathcal F_{t_0}Ft0​​, are at most p0(1−p0)p_0(1-p_0)p0​(1−p0​). The missing amount is the expected remaining conditional variance, also conditional on Ft0\mathcal F_{t_0}Ft0​​. More generally the same argument starts at any grid time, conditional on its information. A probability already near zero or one has little expected revision left.

The budget is an expectation, not a pathwise ceiling. A coherent path can fluctuate more than this number, and large news can cause a large single jump. For a continuous martingale, refining the grid yields quadratic-variation increment [p]T−[p]t0[p]_T-[p]_{t_0}[p]T​−[p]t0​​ and the same conditional expectation identity. That continuous-time formulation uses the usual quadratic-variation theorem Karatzas & Shreve, 1991 and is cited, not proved here; the finite-grid proof above is complete and is what our diagnostics use. An unstopped Brownian motion with a nonzero constant diffusion cannot remain bounded in [0,1][0,1][0,1] almost surely even on a fixed positive horizon.

A pathwise trading calculation¶

The next identity holds for each path, independently of a martingale model.

Proposition 7 (Pathwise trading gain from squared revisions)

Let p0,…,pm∈[0,1]p_0,\ldots,p_m\in[0,1]p0​,…,pm​∈[0,1] be quotes on a finite grid. Put Δpi=pi+1−pi\Delta p_i=p_{i+1}-p_iΔpi​=pi+1​−pi​, V=∑i=0m−1(Δpi)2V=\sum_{i=0}^{m-1}(\Delta p_i)^2V=∑i=0m−1​(Δpi​)2, and hold hi=2(p0−pi)h_i=2(p_0-p_i)hi​=2(p0​−pi​) units over interval iii. Then

G=∑i=0m−12(p0−pi)Δpi,G=V−(pm−p0)2.\begin{gathered} G=\sum_{i=0}^{m-1}2(p_0-p_i)\Delta p_i,\\ G=V-(p_m-p_0)^2. \end{gathered}G=i=0∑m−1​2(p0​−pi​)Δpi​,G=V−(pm​−p0​)2.​
(19)

At each intermediate grid time, accumulated gain is at least −max⁡{p02,(1−p0)2}-\max\{p_0^2,(1-p_0)^2\}−max{p02​,(1−p0​)2}, and ∣hi∣≤2|h_i|\le2∣hi​∣≤2. If the quotes are adapted random variables with deterministic p0p_0p0​ and

V>max⁡{p02,(1−p0)2}almost surelyV>\max\{p_0^2,(1-p_0)^2\} \quad\hbox{almost surely}V>max{p02​,(1−p0​)2}almost surely
(20)

then this predictable strategy has strictly positive terminal gain almost surely. Interpreting this as arbitrage assumes two-way execution at the quotes, no transaction costs, zero financing rate, and self-financing trades.

Proof 9

Expand successive squared distances: (pi+1−p0)2−(pi−p0)2=2(pi−p0)Δpi+(Δpi)2(p_{i+1}-p_0)^2-(p_i-p_0)^2 =2(p_i-p_0)\Delta p_i+(\Delta p_i)^2(pi+1​−p0​)2−(pi​−p0​)2=2(pi​−p0​)Δpi​+(Δpi​)2. Telescoping gives the gain identity at the terminal time and at every intermediate time. Accumulated squared increments are nonnegative, while (pj−p0)2≤max⁡{p02,(1−p0)2}(p_j-p_0)^2\le\max\{p_0^2,(1-p_0)^2\}(pj​−p0​)2≤max{p02​,(1−p0​)2} for each pj∈[0,1]p_j\in[0,1]pj​∈[0,1]. This proves the downside bound, and ∣p0−pi∣≤1|p_0-p_i|\le1∣p0​−pi​∣≤1 bounds the holdings. The strict assumption on VVV makes G>0G>0G>0 almost surely. Adapted quotes make hih_ihi​ measurable at the start of each interval.

This is a sufficient arbitrage condition, much stronger than an unusually large realized VVV on one observed path. In particular the expectation budget p0(1−p0)p_0(1-p_0)p0​(1−p0​) is not this pathwise bound.

Synthetic paths and diagnostics¶

The simulator samples the exact normal transitions of ZZZ, then maps to the share and its terminal-event probability. It includes resolution as the final forecast column. There is no Euler step or clipping scheme used to enforce the martingale. Floating-point CDF values can round to endpoints; subsequent steps use the retained latent coordinate, never an inverse of the rounded share.

The example uses simulate_probit_forecasts and forecast_revision_summary. Rows are 4,000 independent model paths, with 40 transitions, PCG64 seed 1401, initial share 0.54, latent scale 0.8, horizon one, and threshold 1/21/21/2. The diagnostic compares the average squared revisions with the budget and reports its Monte Carlo standard error across independent rows.

Code: exact paths and the revision budget
from xmath.incerto.martingales import (
    simulate_probit_forecasts, forecast_revision_summary,
)

sample = simulate_probit_forecasts(.54, .8, 1, steps=40,
                                  paths=4000, seed=1401)
report = forecast_revision_summary(sample["probability"])
print(f"initial probability: {sample['probability'][0, 0]:.3f}")
print(f"mean terminal outcome: {sample['outcome'].mean():.3f}")
print(f"squared revisions: {report['squared_revision']:.4f}")
print(f"initial budget: {report['initial_budget']:.4f}")
print(f"gap: {report['budget_gap']:.4f}; SE: {report['budget_gap_se']:.4f}")

Output

initial probability: 0.558
mean terminal outcome: 0.560
squared revisions: 0.2481
initial budget: 0.2466
gap: 0.0015; SE: 0.0034

A conditional identity implies E[h(pi)Δpi]=0\mathbb E[h(p_i)\Delta p_i]=0E[h(pi​)Δpi​]=0 for every bounded measurable hhh. The helper reports both h=1h=1h=1 and h(p)=p−1/2h(p)=p-1/2h(p)=p−1/2, with standard errors computed across independent, identically distributed paths separately at each time. These are necessary moment checks, not sufficient tests of the full filtration. The squared-revision budget adds a different necessary check. Standard errors use the usual i.i.d.-row formula; independence alone does not justify pooling rows with different means. Adjacent times on one election path are not independent events. Selecting a statistic after looking at many dates also changes any inferential interpretation.

For a controlled failure, alternate adding and subtracting 0.12 from interior forecasts and clip to [0,1][0,1][0,1], retaining the original initial and terminal reports. This deliberately altered sequence is not the conditional probability under the simulation law. The experiment compares its squared revisions and scores with those of the coherent model; it makes no claim about actual election predictions.

Regenerate all three figures with uv run python demos/incerto/forecast_martingales.py. They use the common figure exporter and fixed seeds. The formulas and finite-grid proofs establish coherence under their stated models; the simulations check numerical implementations and illustrate sampling variation. Marginal calibration, a few small moment residuals, or one smooth-looking forecast path cannot establish dynamic coherence.

Sources and scope¶

SCoFT v4 §14.0.1, pp. 263–264 and §14.1, pp. 266–267 motivate binary valuation; §14.2, pp. 268–269 supplies the bounded-transform construction; §14.3, pp. 269–271 connects probability assessment with scoring; §14.4 and its addendum, pp. 271–273 motivate revision constraints Taleb, 2025. Our derivations distinguish the Gaussian and bounded limits, preserve the transformed threshold, and separate a constant mean from a martingale. Itô’s formula and the continuous quadratic-variation theorem are used as stochastic-calculus prerequisites, not proved here. No empirical forecaster assessment or general claim that uncertainty forces a probability to 1/21/21/2 follows from these calculations.
